item.text: The research pass has now covered the missing areas rather than only repeating the existing notebook: canonical peace terms and implementation, conflict accountability and contrary evidence, political institutions, macro execution and shocks, personal-integrity records, humanitarian delivery, education, and adaptation/recovery. I’m opening the strongest underlying reports now to replace search snippets with precise locator notes, then I’ll assemble the permissive handoff and a complete manifest delta.

Research continuation completed across all eight reviewed chapters for Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia, 2022. No score or score range was assigned.

The workspace remained read-only: `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be modified. The following evidence units are the proposed append-only continuation, beginning at E031.

### 2B — Conflict, peace, and restraint

- **E031 — Pretoria agreement accountability gap.** Amnesty’s 3 November 2022 assessment says the agreement was a positive step but lacked a clear accountability roadmap for abuses by all parties. This supports negotiated restraint while documenting an unresolved accountability deficit; it does not establish Abiy’s personal responsibility for each abuse. Lenses: `2B.3, 2B.7, 2B.9`. [Amnesty](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/11/ethiopia-peace-agreement/), ¶¶61–75.
- **E032 — Agreement terms and federal commitments.** An OHCHR treaty-body submission records the 2 November agreement’s provisions for permanent cessation, civilian protection, humanitarian access, DDR, confidence-building, and restoration of federal authority. The document reports Ethiopian government commitments, not independently verified implementation. Lenses: `2B.3, 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.6, 2B.7`. [OHCHR PDF](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadFile?gId=37433), pp.11–12, ¶¶48–50.
- **E033 — Monitoring and access contrary evidence.** HRW reported that the agreement created an opportunity for monitoring, while much of Tigray still lacked humanitarian access and the government had largely blocked aid before the agreement. This is contrary evidence against treating the agreement as proof of immediate civilian protection. Lenses: `2B.4, 2B.6, 2B.7, 2B.9`. [HRW](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/11/04/ethiopia-truce-needs-robust-rights-monitoring), ¶¶608–626.
- **E034 — Initial post-agreement aid movement.** WFP reported that after the agreement and reopening of four corridors, 96 trucks delivered more than 2,400 metric tons of supplies, but access within Tigray still did not match needs. This is target-period implementation evidence with a documented shortfall. Lenses: `2B.4, 2B.6, 2B.8, 2B.9`. [WFP](https://www.wfp.org/news/wfp-accelerates-humanitarian-operations-northern-ethiopia), ¶¶255–262.

### 3B — Physical integrity and protection

- **E035 — Government-attributed 2022 abuses.** The U.S. State Department’s 2022 country report records credible reports of government unlawful killings, enforced disappearance, torture, arbitrary detention, civilian harm, restrictions on journalists and assembly, and failures to investigate gender-based violence. It is a country-level government-attribution finding, not proof of Abiy’s personal orders. Lenses: `3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.3, 3B.5, 3B.6, 3B.8, 3B.10`. [USDOS report](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089134.html), ¶42.
- **E036 — Independent commission accountability context.** EHRC’s annual report covers June 2022–June 2023 and is based on investigations by its departments and city offices. It is usable for target-period institutional monitoring, but the fiscal-year coverage prevents treating every finding as calendar-year 2022. Lenses: `3B.6, 3B.7, 3B.8, 3B.10`. [EHRC](https://ehrc.org/download/executive-summary-ethiopia-annual-human-rights-situation-report-june-2022-june-2023/), ¶86. Disposition: `context` pending precise calendar-year extraction.
- **E037 — Conflict-era civilian protection failure.** The World Bank’s April 2022 conflict-recovery announcement records widespread physical and sexual violence, destroyed assets, displacement, and limited services for survivors. It documents exposure and a recovery response, not personal attribution to Abiy. Lenses: `3B.1, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.7, 3B.9`. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/04/12/world-bank-supports-ethiopia-s-conflict-affected-communities-targets-over-five-million-people), ¶¶144–148.

### 4B — Political freedom and institutions

- **E038 — Electoral participation and opposition treatment.** Freedom House reports that the 2021 election had improved electoral administration but lacked participation by key groups and included intimidation of opposition parties and media. It also records earlier liberalization under Abiy, making this mixed rather than one-directional evidence. Lenses: `4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.8, 4B.9, 4B.10`. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2022), ¶¶83–88, 128, 132.
- **E039 — Judicial independence and due process.** Freedom House reports political interference in the judiciary, security-force influence over cases involving opposition figures, summary arrests, and weak fair-trial protections, while noting one Federal High Court decision protecting jailed opposition candidates’ electoral participation. Lenses: `4B.2, 4B.5, 4B.6, 4B.9, 4B.10`. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2022), ¶¶223–231.
- **E040 — Emergency powers, media law, and shutdowns.** Freedom House records that the national state of emergency was lifted in February 2022, while emergency powers had enabled media arrests and Tigray’s communications cutoff. It also records reforms to media law. This provides both favorable reform and adverse restriction evidence. Lenses: `4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.5, 4B.9, 4B.10`. [Freedom House Freedom on the Net](https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2022), ¶¶355–358.

### 5B — Economic management and distribution

- **E041 — Macro management under multiple shocks.** IMF staff recorded conflict, drought, COVID-19, and the Ukraine war as drivers of slower growth, inflation, fiscal pressure, and FX shortages. It also recorded government commitments to debt treatment, SOE oversight, public-investment efficiency, FX reform, and private-sector growth. These are agenda and macro-condition evidence, not verified delivery. Lenses: `5B.1, 5B.2, 5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10`. [IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/06/21/pr22216-ethiopia-imf-staff-visit-discusses-reform-plans-and-economic-developments-in-ethiopia), ¶¶243–251.
- **E042 — Food-price and humanitarian-economic deterioration.** WFP reported more than 20 million Ethiopians facing hunger, 43% year-on-year food-price inflation in April 2022, and severe funding gaps that limited nutrition coverage. This is adverse outcome and shock evidence, not solely ruler-attributable performance. Lenses: `5B.3, 5B.5, 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10`. [WFP](https://www.wfp.org/news/conflict-climate-and-soaring-food-prices-push-ethiopia-further-into-hunger-while-wfp-funding-runs), ¶¶262–274.
- **E043 — Safety-net disruption.** Ethiopia’s 2022 Voluntary National Review reports that PSNP implementation stopped in Tigray after June 2021 and was disrupted in Afar and Amhara by conflict, displacement, and destruction. It also records prior improvements in nutrition and agricultural productivity, but warns that drought, conflict, prices, and input costs threatened reversal. Lenses: `5B.2, 5B.5, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10`. [Ethiopia VNR PDF](https://hlpf.un.org/sites/default/files/vnrs/2022/VNR%202022%20Ethiopia%20Report.pdf), pp.40–42.

### 6B — Human development and services

- **E044 — Target-year emergency health delivery.** UNICEF reports that in 2022 it supported maternal care, emergency drug distribution, vaccine cold chains, mobile health teams, rehabilitation of 85 health centres, measles campaigns, and health services for conflict- and drought-affected populations across Tigray, Amhara, Afar, Somali, Oromia, and SNNP. Delivery was partner-supported and cannot be assigned personally to Abiy. Lenses: `6B.1, 6B.2, 6B.5, 6B.6, 6B.8, 6B.9`. [UNICEF PDF](https://www.unicef.org/media/134196/file/UNICEF%20Ethiopia%20Humanitarian%20Situation%20Report%20No.%2012%20-%20January%20-%20December%202022.pdf), p.3.
- **E045 — National nutrition-program launch.** Ethiopia launched a $30 million nutrition programme in July 2022, implemented with the Ministry of Health, UNICEF, humanitarian partners, and private-sector actors, targeting maternal malnutrition, child wasting, and stunting. This establishes stated priorities and implementation structure, not verified national outcomes. Lenses: `6B.4, 6B.6, 6B.7, 6B.8`. [UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/government-ethiopia-launches-30-million-nutrition-programme-reduce-maternal), ¶¶57, 73–76.
- **E046 — Education equity and quality constraints.** The World Bank’s 2022 education expenditure and institutional review reports increased access over the prior decade but says COVID-19 and political unrest increased unfinished learning, reduced participation, and inequality. It supports a mixed education record, with no direct Abiy-specific execution finding. Lenses: `6B.3, 6B.5, 6B.8, 6B.9, 6B.10`. [World Bank PEIR](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099615206172211408), publication date 31 May 2022.
- **E047 — Drought-response delay.** The New Humanitarian reported delayed livestock vaccination, fodder distribution, and drinking-water interventions in drought-affected southeast Ethiopia while federal and donor attention focused on the northern conflict. This is adverse delivery and prioritization evidence, but regional and donor responsibility remain mixed. Lenses: `6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.6, 6B.8, 6B.9, 6B.10`. [The New Humanitarian](https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/news/2022/03/24/funding-shortages-thwart-ethiopia-drought-response-as-crises-multiply), ¶¶60–89.

### 7B — Personal integrity

- **E048 — Federal anti-corruption committee and official arrests.** Ethiopia created a national anti-corruption committee on 17 November 2022; officials reported investigations and arrests involving alleged financial plundering, land grabbing, procurement, and other corruption. This is evidence of an official anti-corruption response and systemic corruption exposure, not evidence of Abiy’s personal corruption or integrity. Lenses: `7B.3, 7B.5, 7B.6, 7B.8, 7B.10`. Disposition: `context`. [ENA](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_40822), ¶¶56–61, 77–79.
- **E049 — Addis Ababa land-corruption proceedings.** A contemporaneous report records the Ministry of Justice pursuing a city land-administration official, revocation of council immunity, and allegations concerning land distribution. It also records an official apology concerning condominium allocation. No personal nexus to Abiy is shown. Lenses: `7B.4, 7B.5, 7B.6, 7B.8, 7B.10`. Disposition: `context`. [Borkena](https://borkena.com/2022/10/14/ethiopian-court-going-after-a-city-councilor-over-alleged-corruption/), ¶¶105–121.
- **Chapter shortfall:** Searches did not recover a defensible 2022 personal asset disclosure, personal financial finding, court judgment against Abiy, or independently verified evidence of personal enrichment, favoritism, concealment, or obstruction. The required personal-integrity nexus remains absent.

### 8B — Effectiveness and execution

- **E050 — Government recovery framework.** Ethiopia’s Ministry of Finance presented a government-led reconstruction and recovery framework for Amhara, Afar, Tigray, Benishangul-Gumuz, and parts of Oromia, while development partners raised concerns about peace, humanitarian access, and rights violations. This is a stated implementation plan with external reservations. Lenses: `8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.7, 8B.8, 8B.9, 8B.10`. [Ministry of Finance](https://www.mofed.gov.et/blog/dialogue-between-ministry-finance-and-head-agencies-development-partners-relation-reconstruction-and-recovery-plan-conflict-affected-regions/), ¶¶88–94.
- **E051 — Conflict-recovery project outputs.** The World Bank approved a $300 million conflict-recovery grant targeting more than five million people, with mobile education, health, water, sanitation, and GBV services. This establishes externally financed delivery infrastructure, not completed outcomes or Abiy-specific management. Lenses: `8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.4, 8B.5, 8B.8`. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/04/12/world-bank-supports-ethiopia-s-conflict-affected-communities-targets-over-five-million-people), ¶¶144–148.
- **E052 — Post-agreement logistics execution and limits.** WFP documented reopened corridors, deliveries, fuel movement, and resumed flights after the November agreement, while stating that assistance still did not reach all vulnerable people. This supports partial implementation with a material coverage gap. Lenses: `8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.4, 8B.5, 8B.8, 8B.9`. [WFP](https://www.wfp.org/news/wfp-accelerates-humanitarian-operations-northern-ethiopia), ¶¶255–262.
- **E053 — Agriculture intervention outcome evidence with period limitation.** A 2022 FAO paper finds that Ethiopian agricultural interventions implemented from 2011–2016 were associated with higher yields and improved food security, especially for vulnerable households. This is useful persistent programme evidence, but it is not a 2022 intervention or Abiy-specific execution finding. Lenses: `8B.3, 8B.4, 8B.5, 8B.8, 8B.9`. Disposition: `context`. [FAO](https://www.fao.org/agrifood-economics/publications/detail/en/c/1622675/), ¶¶27–40.

### Chapter 1B disposition

No additional defensible unit was recovered beyond E017–E028. E029 remains `discovery_only`; E030 remains `rejected`. The chapter still lacks independently verified cyber incidents, nuclear-material control records, catastrophic-risk exercises, near misses, remediation, and Abiy-specific authorization evidence.

### Bias and contrary-search findings

- Favorable evidence recovered: peace agreement, restored humanitarian corridors, anti-corruption investigations, emergency health delivery, nutrition programming, education and recovery plans, and earlier political liberalization.
- Adverse evidence recovered: accountability gaps, blocked or incomplete humanitarian access, conflict-related abuses, judicial interference, opposition intimidation, shutdowns, inflation, safety-net disruption, drought-response delays, and incomplete service coverage.
- Closed-system silence remains unsafe because Tigray communications restrictions and access limitations suppress reporting.
- Official claims and partner-financed programmes were not counted as independent proof of ruler-specific success.
- Country-level outcomes were not converted into personal attribution.
- Chapter 7B remains a genuine evidence shortfall, not a negative integrity finding.

The continuation therefore improves every reviewed chapter, but does not close the major attribution and implementation gaps.
